text: This lesson builds the real workbook. Power Query imports the CSV export as a refreshable table, which means a newer export can be loaded later without rebuilding anything on top of it.
A PivotTable gives Finance a territory-by-category breakdown, built entirely independently from a flat CSV, using nothing but Excel's own summarization.

The real check Finance cares about is narrower: one SUMIFS formula totaling an entire quarter, using a lower and upper date bound. It reads exactly the way a calendar quarter gets described in ordinary conversation.

This formula looks completely reasonable — it compiles, it references real columns, and it produces a number. That's exactly why it has to be checked against the other two deliverables, not just trusted on sight. Next lesson does that check.
